entries.definition: Deeds — not a synonym for obedience. A work becomes obedience when it executes a legitimate command; it becomes disobedience when the command or deed conflicts with God's command. Romans 4 uses the laborer's work offered for wages and debt; James 2 uses Abraham's work as faith made visible. Complete obedience still earns no wage: the servant has only done his duty.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught: in Paul's salvation texts, “works” broadly includes human obedience and effort set against faith; good works then follow salvation as its fruit and evidence.
entries.citations: (Ex 18:20; Ps 111:7; Mic 6:16; Luke 17:7-10; Rom 4:4-5; Jas 2:21-22) · see Love, Knowing, Faith & Belief, ch. 6, for faith and works, and The End of the Law for Paul's works, wages, and duty vocabulary

entries.definition: Paul's phrase for deeds considered in relation to law. It is not a synonym for obedience and does not identify one unchanging class of deeds. The surrounding passage may identify God's law, a circumcision-party application, or leave the particular acts unnamed. What remains consistent is the rejected claim made for those deeds: they cannot purchase justification, produce the Spirit, establish covenant standing, or place God in debt. The context identifies the work; the phrase denies it as the purchase price.
entries.citations: (Rom 3:20, 28; 9:32 KJV/TR; Gal 2:16; 3:2, 5, 10) · see The End of the Law
